column4: An intended operation or component is absent, disabled, stubbed, or replaced by placeholder behavior.
column5: Explicit implementation requests, empty methods, missing model components, or inactive intended features.
column6: Use S02 for additional variants of an already supported operation; S04 for persistence; S07 for missing tests.

column4: An existing operation supports only a subset of required input forms, algorithms, entities, dimensions, or execution modes.
column5: Explicit unsupported variants, restrictive assumptions, or requests to generalize case coverage.
column6: Do not infer missing support merely from an untested case; use S07 or S20 for verification alone.

column4: The source identifies a concrete mismatch between implemented processing and an intended semantic requirement.
column5: Incorrect selection, alignment, counting, transformations, or a stated wrong algorithmic component.
column6: Use S20 for questions without a supported mismatch, S06 for exceptional-input handling, and S19 for provisional approximations.

column4: Required output, metadata, identifiers, persisted state, or provenance is omitted, lossy, unstable, or inadequately represented.
column5: Missing save/load behavior, missing output fields, unstable indices, lossy metadata conversion, and serialization-format changes.
column6: Use S14 for diagnostic presentation, S12 for general interface redesign, and S16 when the central concern is external compatibility.

column4: A required validity, consistency, integrity, or authorization check is absent or incomplete.
column5: Input-schema checks, cross-input consistency, configuration validation, hash checking, and access preconditions.
column6: Use S06 for response to failure after it occurs; S07 for tests; retain uncertainty when a check already partly exists.

column4: Exceptional states, numerical limits, invalid inputs, or failures lack adequate recovery, reporting, or protection.
column5: Zero denominators, overflow range, None values, retries, missing error branches, and poor exception diagnostics.
column6: Use S05 for ordinary precondition checks and S20 when only the desirability of a nonexceptional behavior is questioned.

column4: Tests, assertions, fixtures, or coverage are missing, disabled, weak, or require adaptation.
column5: Explicit requests for tests, failed or skipped tests, absent value assertions, and unverified test tolerances.
column6: Do not claim a production defect solely from a test gap; use S08 for empirical model/protocol evaluation.

column4: Modeling, preprocessing, sampling, or evaluation choices need empirical assessment, broader measurement, or a sounder evaluation protocol.
column5: Architecture experiments, missing evaluation metrics, inadequate model results, train/test reuse, and sampling balance for evaluation.
column6: Use S07 for software tests and S20 for unverified local semantic assumptions without an empirical comparison request.

column4: Existing processing incurs unnecessary execution cost or could exploit parallelism, optimized primitives, caching, or reduced repeated work.
column5: Explicit slowness, unnecessary full sorting, repeated computation, host/device transfer, and proposed parallelization.
column6: Use S10 for storage/retention pressure; do not assume a proposed optimization has a measured benefit.

column4: Data representation, eager loading, or retained intermediates impose unnecessary memory or serialized-size cost.
column5: Sparse data stored densely, eager corpus loading, retained graph arrays, and oversized serialized graphs.
column6: Use S18 for ownership correctness and S09 for runtime cost without a stated footprint concern.

column4: Code organization, dependency structure, duplicated logic, or implementation complexity calls for restructuring or reuse.
column5: Extract/move helpers, remove circular coupling, use existing abstractions, simplify dense logic, and replace magic identifiers.
column6: Use S12 for public naming/contracts; do not attribute functional failure to a refactoring request alone.

column4: Names, types, parameter representations, API exposure, or abstraction boundaries inadequately communicate or coordinate intended use.
column5: Renaming, contradictory return contracts, redundant parameters, overloaded flags, generic annotations, and public API requests.
column6: Use S15 for selectable configuration and S11 for internal code placement or duplication.

column4: Explanations, docstrings, usage examples, tutorials, or format specifications need creation or correction.
column5: Explicit documentation requests and inadequate representative examples.
column6: Use S14 for runtime diagnostics and S22 for explanatory comments that do not request documentation changes.

column4: Logs, plots, runtime feedback, or displayed analysis details are missing, misleading, or insufficiently useful.
column5: Missing visualizations, suppressed logging, diagnostic metadata, and loss of detail in plots.
column6: Use S04 for durable analytical records and S07 for tests that merely log instead of assert.

column4: Fixed values, environment-specific paths, or poorly derived defaults should become selectable, inferred, or consistently propagated.
column5: Hard-coded thresholds, resource counts, split ratios, dimensions, paths, missing defaults, and configuration precedence.
column6: Use S20 for uncertainty about a value without a request for configurability; fixed values alone do not establish debt.

column4: Dependency versions, platform behavior, external APIs, or package integration constrain functionality or require adaptation.
column5: Upstream bugs, missing external APIs, environment-specific failures, compatibility shims, and dependency migrations.
column6: Use S17 for scheduled retirement of transitional interfaces and S11 for internal dependency organization.

column4: Temporary, deprecated, redundant, or debugging code is retained pending removal or migration completion.
column5: Scheduled API/test removal, old aliases, debug prints, migration scaffolding, and explicit unused-code removal.
column6: Do not imply removal is already safe when the source makes it conditional; use S16 for a still-required compatibility mechanism.

column4: State ownership, lifecycle ordering, concurrent access, scheduling, or cross-worker coordination needs correction or redesign.
column5: Thread-local state, file races, resource sessions, blocking execution, stale training state, shared-layer identity, and state propagation order.
column6: Use S10 for memory pressure alone and S20 for an unresolved question without a stated coordination obligation.

column4: A local approximation, forced assumption, fallback, or brittle convention substitutes for a better justified general solution.
column5: Explicit hacks, arbitrary first-match selection, patched malformed spans, fixed substitute values, and fragile naming conventions.
column6: Use S16 for external-compatibility-driven workarounds; preserve whether the current workaround is already effective.

column4: The author questions correctness, necessity, interpretation, or design semantics without enough evidence to establish a specific defect.
column5: Questions about formulas, boundary conventions, unnecessary operations, ambiguous defaults, and possibly stale TODOs.
column6: Use a concrete substantive code when the intended change is explicit; retain the question instead of converting it into a confirmed fault.

column4: A revision marker exists but available material does not establish a sufficiently specific substantive concern.
column5: Bare TODO/FIXME, opaque experiment markers, unspecified bugs, and unclear inactive alternatives.
column6: Do not use when surrounding context identifies a concrete missing operation or concern; this records evidence limits, not a defect type.

column4: The selected annotation describes implemented behavior, an existing safeguard, or an instructional task without establishing unresolved production work.
column5: Already implemented operations, explanatory needed-for comments, equivalent implementations, and exercise placeholders.
column6: Do not count this as confirmed technical debt; use a substantive code when an explicit remaining change is supported.
